summary: An overview of this week's technology developments, highlighting major advancements in artificial intelligence, developer tools, and privacy-focused mobile operating systems.

items.title: Hugging Face reportedly in talks to be acquired for $13B
items.summary: Hugging Face is reportedly in talks for an acquisition that would value the AI platform at approximately $13 billion. However, the founders' sense of responsibility to the community has raised doubts about whether a sale will actually occur.

items.title: OpenAI is building AI agents for everything. Will everyone use them?
items.summary: OpenAI is actively developing AI agents designed to assist with a wide range of tasks from software engineering to everyday activities. This initiative represents a major push by the frontier lab to bring agentic AI technology to the general public.

items.title: Valor, Point72 back General Intuition at $6B valuation as AI startup pushes into robotics
items.summary: AI startup General Intuition is in discussions to raise funding at a $6 billion pre-money valuation from investors including Valor Ventures and Point72 Ventures. The company plans to use the capital to advance its foundation models that train AI agents to navigate physical space and time.

items.title: De-Googled GrapheneOS is coming to Motorola’s foldables next year
items.summary: The privacy-focused, open-source Android operating system GrapheneOS has announced plans to expand official support to Motorola smartphones next year. This expansion will initially target traditional flagship models before rolling out to Motorola's foldable devices.

items.title: Raspberry Pi shares its official tutorial for making a cyberdeck
items.summary: Raspberry Pi has released an official guide to help users build their own custom, portable cyberdecks using recycled or thrifted components. The tutorial capitalizes on a viral social media trend while offering a creative project amidst rising component costs.
